A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLUS research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–K are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original reward-model experiments on Pets, UltraFeedback, and PRISM, together with ablations, robustness tests, and GPT-4 personalization results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in the main text and appendices, including reward-model accuracy and personalized response win rates.

M1.justification: The alternating summarizer/reward-model training and personalization procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 rewords reward computation and omits explicit advantage computation and equation references, but Section 4 retains the same rewards, GAE calculation, and PPO/NLL objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pets, Pets OOD, UltraFeedback-P2/P4, and PRISM. Coverage of flexible user contexts, held-out conversations and users, personalized LLM judging, and response generation is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain BTL, DPL, VPL, ICL, PLUS-untrained, and oracle models. Fixed-model and GPT-4o summarizer ablations, larger ICL models, and default GPT-4 response comparators also retain their participation.

E3.justification: The versions report identical data splits, sample counts, context sampling, model configurations, metrics, and training settings. PRISM evaluation procedures and the controlled response ordering described in Appendix K are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The co-adaptation ablations, Pets OOD robustness test, flexible-input comparisons, larger-model ICL analysis, and PRISM generalization analysis are retained. Appendix F reformats the same personalization examples without adding or removing an analytical finding.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains means and two-sided 95% t-intervals over three seeds where reported, with single-seed results otherwise. Table 2 retains its three-seed reporting. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains PLUS Pets OOD accuracy of 93.67 ± 9.96, Table 8 retains PRISM accuracy of 62.9%, and Figure 4 retains GPT-4o win rates of 72% versus 28%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same probability definitions, joint objective, reward formulation, GAE calculation, and PPO loss. Algorithm 1's shortened wording does not revise the mathematical reasoning, and no theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions and claim scope: learned textual user summaries, co-adaptation, improved preference prediction, robustness, flexible inputs, and personalization of proprietary models without further fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of co-adaptation, summary usefulness, and PRISM generalization remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning training sensitivity, sparse heterogeneous user data, and poor reward-model generalization to unseen PRISM users, alongside the same privacy discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation information, hardware, hyperparameters, dataset sizes, and prompts remain unchanged, as does the code link in the reproducibility statement. Updating the OpenRLHF citation year does not document a different software implementation or experimental setting.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. OpenRLHF's author list and year are updated, and the Lee statistics reference receives a revised title and access date; these remain the same cited sources rather than new related work.

P1.justification: v4 adds author email addresses, simplifies Algorithm 1's wording, promotes Ethics Statement and Reproducibility to standalone headings, and updates bibliographic metadata. The substantive prose and section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block changes from three columns to two, Figure 4 moves from page 9 to page 10, and appendix tables reflow. Appendix F replaces green highlights with bold emphasis and tighter spacing, fixing a quotation extending into the margin. Figure images and table contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves readability by placing Figure 4 beside the response-generation discussion and fixing awkward spacing and a margin overflow in Appendix F. Algorithm 1 loses useful equation references, but its mathematical explanation remains in Section 4. The gains are limited to presentation; scientific content and evidential support are unchanged.
